clue.text: That's right — I am, according to country-folk, a writer

parts.note: sc., short for the Latin scilicet, means 'that is' or 'namely'
in rustic dialect speech 'I am' becomes 'I be', so 'am' is said as be

explanation.surface: A rural speaker agrees that they are indeed an author.
explanation.walkthrough: SC (scilicet, 'that is') is the dictionary abbreviation that turns 'That's' into letters; the stage yokel's 'I be' supplies the final BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a copyist or clerk, someone whose trade is putting words on paper.

clue.text: Dark yellow cocked hat

parts.note: sombre means dark or gloomy

indicators.note: cocked, tilted upward, turns the word for yellow upside down in a down answer

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: A dull yellow hat worn at an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: The sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Poem — it may be on a -high-flown plane

definitions.meaning: a short verse form with refrains, also spelt rondel

definitions.text: it may be on a -high-flown plane
definitions.meaning: the circular marking painted on a military aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: A roundel is a rondeau-like verse form and also the ring-shaped insignia on RAF aircraft.

clue.text: Try and be relaxed about second witness

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for second
relaxed suggests the letters of try and be are loosened into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to stay calm about a moment's delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'witness' looks like a verb but is the noun definition; 'relaxed' loosens the three words into a new order and 'about' wraps them round the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander is an onlooker, someone present to see an event happen.

clue.text: Accents make an appearance in. European river

indicators.note: the appearance word is placed in the middle of the river's name

parts.note: the Ems is a river in north-west Germany
a phase is one appearance in a cycle, as with the phases of the moon

explanation.surface: Stresses are said to show up in a river on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Accents and stresses are the same idea: the special weight placed on a syllable or point.

clue.text: Celebrate what you can do with hating

definitions.meaning: have a party lasting into the small hours

definitions.text: what you can do with hating
definitions.meaning: taking the word hating as 'it', its letters can be made into 'a night'

explanation.surface: Throw a party: that is how to turn hatred into fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is wordplay as a definition: 'hating' rearranged spells A NIGHT, so you can literally make a night of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a night of it is to celebrate by carrying on late into the evening.

clue.text: Walker for President, in time

indicators.note: the president's nickname goes in the abbreviation for time

parts.note: hr is short for hour, a measure of time
Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A US presidential candidate called Walker, in office at the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiker is someone who walks long distances in the countryside.

clue.text: Deprived of oxygen, collapse - .moved for medical aid

indicators.note: moved signals that the remaining letters shift into a new order
deprived of means the word collapse loses its oxygen

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Starved of oxygen, a patient collapses and is moved to get help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deprived of' drops O from COLLAPSE, leaving CLLAPSE; 'moved' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is a surgeon's small knife, an instrument of medical help.

clue.text: Ostentatious display, despite cut involving money

indicators.note: involving means the cut word wraps round the money letter

parts.note: a slash is a cut
p, for penny or pence, stands for money

explanation.surface: A showy display, in spite of the spending cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a splash is to show off in a conspicuous way.

clue.text: Sensation! What Housewife Concealed!.

definitions.meaning: the tingling felt when a numb limb recovers
a housewife (pronounced hussif) is a small sewing kit holding needlework items

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline about a scandal at home.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'housewife' is an old British name for a pocket sewing kit, which conceals sharp needlework items.
explanation.definitionFit: The tingling feeling is called this, and it names what a sewing kit holds.

clue.text: A rest for painter damages credit

parts.note: to maul something is to batter or damage it
tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: An artist's support stick harms one's standing at the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter steadies the brush hand on this padded stick, a support held across the canvas.

clue.text: Bird circling around a village.

indicators.note: the bird's letters go round the single letter a
around means the whole result is turned to read backwards

parts.note: a lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: A bird flies in circles round a small settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts A inside LARK to give LAARK; 'around' then turns that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In southern Africa a kraal is a traditional settlement of huts, often fenced for livestock.

clue.text: Angles boy's right to the head

indicators.note: the letter for right is shifted to the front of the word

parts.note: Adrian's: Adrian is a boy's name, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A lad's entitlement to be in charge, phrased as geometry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the head' moves the R of ADRIAN'S to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The radian is a unit of angular measure, so radians are angles measured in that unit.

clue.text: Incidentally, after start of attack, stay well back

indicators.note: start of means only the first letter of the word attack is used

parts.note: a prop is a support or stay

indicators.note: back means the word for well is read backwards

parts.note: so, as in 'so, what now?', can stand for well

explanation.surface: In passing, after an attack begins, you should keep well to the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SO (well) into OS at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos, used as an adverb, means by the way, introducing a remark in passing.

clue.text: Controlled with lines

definitions.meaning: describing paper marked with straight lines

explanation.definitionFit: Ruled means both governed by a sovereign and printed with parallel guide lines, as exercise paper is.

clue.text: Used by beautician or, -separately, by carpenter

definitions.meaning: a manicurist's tool for shaping fingernails
taken as two words, a carpenter uses both a nail and a file

explanation.surface: One tool for the salon, two for the workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Joined, it is the emery board of manicure; split into its two halves, each is woodworking kit.

clue.text: Coast 'where : differences are. .apparent in female fish

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go in between the female and fish letters

parts.note: an eel is a fish

indicators.note: the letters of where show differences, appearing in a new order

explanation.surface: A seaside spot where female fish look unlike each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coast' poses as the seaside but is the verb; 'differences are apparent' signals a rearrangement, and 'in' sets it between the female and the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast on a bicycle is to roll along without pedalling.

clue.text: Keep quiet about suit

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction for quiet
re means about or concerning
to serve is to suit or be suitable

explanation.surface: Stay silent about a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: P is piano, the musical direction for soft.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve is to maintain or save something from harm.

clue.text: Make economies — dig another hole

definitions.meaning: taken in two parts, to excavate a ditch over again

explanation.definitionFit: To retrench is to cut costs; split as re-trench it means to dig a trench once more.

clue.text: Shout out various numbers in the course of test

indicators.note: a further numeral is dropped in at another point during the test word
the first Roman numerals are put in the test word

parts.note: an exam is a test
with numbers, various Roman numerals are meant: CL is 150
I is 1 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Yell out a number of answers during an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'various numbers' are Roman numerals, CL and I, slotted into EXAM at two different points rather than as one block.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly.

clue.text: Always gets doctor in in the aftermath of a fire

indicators.note: the word for always takes the doctor's letters inside it
the word for always takes the doctor's letters inside it

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor is forever called in once a blaze has died down.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER is a poetic spelling of ever; MB (Bachelor of Medicine) is a British medical degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing coal left smouldering is what remains once the flames have gone.

clue.text: A bitter upset for head of church

indicators.note: upset means the letters of a bitter are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A churchman is served a disappointing glass of ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges BITTER to BIRETT, and the A ends the answer; bitter is also a British beer, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The biretta is the square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy.

clue.text: A maiden treated and entertained

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
used as in 'used badly', meaning treated

explanation.surface: A young woman was looked after and kept happy.
explanation.walkthrough: M for maiden comes from cricket scoring, where a maiden over yields no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Amused means diverted or kept happily occupied.

clue.text: Grim : staff outside a nationalised undertaking

indicators.note: the staff word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a mace is a ceremonial staff
BR, British Rail, was the state-owned railway in Britain

explanation.surface: A gloomy picture of officials standing outside a state-run company.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, Britain's railway when it was a state-owned enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means gruesome and death-haunted, a darker shade of grim.

clue.text: Peer, but find nothing in store

indicators.note: nothing goes in the store word

parts.note: a barn is a farm store
O, zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A nobleman searches the warehouse and turns up nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a member of the peerage, the lowest rank of British nobility.

clue.text: Where nurses go ahead

definitions.meaning: read as two words, nurses work on hospital wards

explanation.surface: Nurses march forward onto the hospital floors.
explanation.definitionFit: Onwards means forward; as 'on wards' it is where hospital nurses spend their shifts.

clue.text: Into the lead I step

indicators.note: the letter I goes into the word for the lead

parts.note: the star is the lead role in a show

explanation.surface: Someone stepping into a leading part.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is a single step in a flight.

clue.text: The queen's favourite isle? Crete, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Was Her Majesty's best-loved island perhaps Crete?
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was the favourite of Elizabeth I; 'possibly' rearranges ISLE CRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Dudley, created Earl of Leicester, was famously the courtier closest to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Short skirt pretty girl's about to make shorter

indicators.note: the girl's word goes about, around, the skirt

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: An attractive young woman in a miniskirt is about to take up the hem.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to reduce or lessen, making something smaller.

clue.text: About. to' go and split up

parts.note: c., short for circa, means about
to leave is to go away

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of leaving and breaking up.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa) is the standard abbreviation for about.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split apart, as with an axe through wood.
